name: Data
description: Look at a table, ask it questions in SQL, summarise a column, draw a chart, convert a spreadsheet. Works on CSV files (comma, semicolon or tab separated; a BOM is fine). The CSV is imported into a private temporary database and the SQL runs in sqlite's read-only safe mode (it can only read that one table, called t); your file is never changed. Answers are markdown tables, charts are SVG. In the extra-arguments box a column is a name (use _ for a space), or a number (1 = the first column).

presets.label: First rows
presets.description: The first rows of a CSV. Extra argument: how many (default 10).

presets.label: Describe every column
presets.description: Per column: rows, empty, distinct values, min, max, and for numeric columns the sum and mean.

presets.label: SQL query
presets.description: Any SELECT on the file; the table is called t. Extra argument: the SQL, for example  SELECT city, COUNT(*) FROM t GROUP BY city. Read-only: nothing can be changed or written.

presets.label: Column statistics
presets.description: Count, sum, mean, min, max of one column. Extra argument: the column.

presets.label: Most frequent values
presets.description: The values of one column by how often they occur. Extra arguments: the column, and how many to show (default 20).

presets.label: Make a database file
presets.description: Writes FILE.db beside the CSV (table t) so you can query it again and again. Never replaces an existing file.

presets.label: Spreadsheet to CSV
presets.description: The first sheet of an .xlsx, .xls or .ods file as CSV (LibreOffice, headless).

presets.label: Bar chart
presets.description: Extra arguments: the category column, the number column (leave it out to count rows), then a title. Repeated categories are added up; at most 30 bars.

presets.label: Line chart
presets.description: Extra arguments: the x column, the y column, then a title. Numbers are sorted along x; text keeps its order.

presets.label: Scatter plot
presets.description: Extra arguments: the x column, the y column (both numbers), then a title.

presets.label: Histogram
presets.description: Extra arguments: the number column, and optionally how many bins (5-40; the default follows the number of rows).
